# statnnet

`statnnet` provides statistically based selection and regression-style
interpretation for small, single-hidden-layer neural networks fitted with
`nnet`. It can select an unpenalised Gaussian model using information criteria,
or augment an existing supported `nnet` fit.

## Installation

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("andrew-mcinerney/statnnet")
```

## Basic workflow

The primary workflow chooses input terms and hidden-layer size using multiple
random initialisations, then augments the selected fit with diagnostics and
regression-style summaries:

```{r data, message=FALSE}
library(nnet)
library(statnnet)

data("auto_mpg", package = "statnnet")
analysis_data <- auto_mpg
continuous_variables <- c(
  "mpg", "displacement", "horsepower", "weight",
  "acceleration", "model_year"
)
analysis_data[continuous_variables] <- lapply(
  analysis_data[continuous_variables],
  function(x) as.numeric(scale(x))
)
```

```{r selection, eval=FALSE}
selection <- select_nnet(
  mpg ~ displacement + horsepower + weight + acceleration +
    model_year + origin,
  data = analysis_data,
  max_size = 3,
  n_starts = 10,
  seed = 2026
)

selection
selection_path(selection)
model <- statnnet(selection)
```

An existing supported fit can also be augmented directly:

```{r example, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
set.seed(2026)
fit <- nnet(
  mpg ~ weight + model_year + origin,
  data = analysis_data,
  size = 1,
  linout = TRUE,
  decay = 0.1,
  Hess = TRUE,
  maxit = 1000,
  trace = FALSE
)

model <- statnnet(
  fit,
  data = analysis_data,
  response = "continuous"
)

model
anova(model)
```

`summary(model)` returns structured average observed-row predictive effects and
grouped Wald-type summaries. `pce()` and `plot()` provide finite-difference
partial covariate effects with delta-method or simulation uncertainty.

```{r pce, eval=FALSE}
summary(model)
pce(model, "weight")
plot(model, "weight")
plot_network(model, annotate = "p_value")
```

These summaries describe the fitted response function. They are conditional
on the chosen network and are not post-selection or causal inference.

## Inference guardrails

An available covariance matrix means that the fitted Hessian passed the
package's numerical checks; it does not establish calibrated Wald tests or
confidence intervals. The Gaussian-response simulation evidence motivating
these summaries supports small, parsimonious networks, including keeping the
hidden layer no larger than the fitted input layer. `statnnet()` records the
hidden-to-input ratio and warns when the number of hidden nodes exceeds the
number of fitted input nodes.

All Wald p-values and delta-method intervals are approximate and conditional
on the fitted architecture, penalty, and local optimum. The cited calibration
studies concern continuous Gaussian responses. Binary-response calculations
are available for exploring a fitted response surface, but their frequentist
calibration has not been established by the package authors.
